melasma.name: Melasma
melasma.tagline: Gradually breaks down chronic pigments located in the epidermis and dermis
melasma.intro: Melasma is a chronic pigment that does not disappear at once, as melanin is distributed simultaneously in the epidermis and dermis. To reduce recurrence, it is necessary to perform toning tailored to the depth of the pigment along with skin barrier management rather than a single treatment.
melasma.approach: 1) Gradually break down the pigment with Clarity II or Fotona StarWalker toning, 2) Additional care for deep dermal pigments using Long-pulsed or multi-wavelength mode, 3) Suppress recurrence by combining moisturizing and sun protection for skin barrier recovery.
recommendedFor: Individuals with symmetrical brown pigments on both cheeks and forehead
Individuals whose pigmentation has darkened after pregnancy, childbirth, or hormonal changes
Individuals who frequently experience recurrence after existing treatments
Individuals concerned about both epidermal and dermal pigmentation
Individuals who can receive regular maintenance toning

faq.q: Does it disappear all at once?
faq.a: Melasma is a chronic pigment and does not disappear at once. Typically, it is lightened through gradual toning every 3 weeks for 5 to 10 sessions, after which maintenance treatments are necessary.
Key measures include sun protection (daily SPF 50+), minimizing friction, and regular maintenance toning.
Pain is alleviated with anesthetic cream. Slight redness lasts for 1 to 2 days.
Primarily, Clarity II dual-wavelength toning and Fotona StarWalker multi-wavelength toning are combined according to the depth of the pigment.

freckles.name: Freckles · Dark Spots · Seborrheic Keratosis
freckles.tagline: Precisely remove with a laser tailored to the depth of the lesions
freckles.intro: Freckles, dark spots (lentigo), and seborrheic keratosis are pigmented lesions located at the epidermis-dermis boundary. Depending on the depth and type of each lesion, different laser wavelengths and modes are selected for effective removal in one session.
freckles.approach: 1) Precisely decompose epidermal pigments with Q-Switched mode, 2) For raised lesions like seborrheic keratosis, additional care with fractional mode or CO2, 3) Thorough UV protection is implemented after the procedure to prevent pigmentation.
recommendedFor: Individuals with multiple freckles on the face and hands
Individuals with dark spots that have darkened over the years
Individuals who want to see results in one treatment
Individuals with various types of pigmented lesions
Individuals seeking precise laser treatment

faq.q: Does it disappear in one session?
faq.a: Freckles and small dark spots show results in 1-2 sessions, but seborrheic keratosis may require 3-5 sessions depending on depth.
A fine scab will form on the treated area for about a week and will fall off naturally.
The risk is low due to precise output control, but UV protection and moisturizing are essential after the procedure.
Freckles may recur with UV exposure, while seborrheic keratosis rarely recurs once removed.

resistant-pigment.name: Resistant Pigment
resistant-pigment.tagline: Step-by-step care for deep dermal pigments such as Ota and ABNOM
resistant-pigment.intro: Resistant pigments located in the deep dermis, such as Ota nevus and ABNOM (Acquired Bilateral Nevus of Ota-like Macules), do not easily fade with regular toning. They are gradually lightened over a long period using a combination of long-wavelength lasers and multi-modes.
resistant-pigment.approach: 1) Reach deep dermal pigments with Long-pulsed Nd:YAG, 2) Additional breakdown with Q-Switched mode, 3) Assist dermal regeneration with Secret RF, 4) Proceed with a long-term plan of 10-20 sessions at intervals of 3-5 weeks.
recommendedFor: Individuals with bluish-gray pigments on the cheeks and temples (Ota nevus, ABNOM)
Those who have not seen results from regular toning for years
Individuals who can follow a long-term treatment plan
Those concerned about deep dermal pigments
Individuals who can have regular monitoring by medical staff

faq.a: Depending on the depth of the lesions, more than 10-20 sessions may be required, conducted at intervals of 3-5 weeks.
It will significantly lighten, but complete removal is often difficult. Realistic goals are set during the initial consultation.
Anesthesia cream is applied. There may be a slight sting during treatment of the deeper layers.

faq.q: Can it be combined with other treatments?
faq.a: It is effective when combined with moisturizing, sun protection, and skin barrier care.

ota-cafe.name: Ota · Café-au-lait Spot
ota-cafe.tagline: Precise stepwise treatment of congenital pigment lesions
ota-cafe.intro: Ota nevus (congenital dermal melanocytosis) and café-au-lait spots are congenital pigment lesions. Unlike regular toning, they require long-term stepwise treatment with a multi-wavelength laser that reaches deep dermal pigments.
ota-cafe.approach: 1) Precisely break down the melanocytes in the dermis with Q-Switched multi-wavelength laser, 2) Care for deeper layers with Long-pulsed mode, 3) Lighten the lesions through stepwise treatment of more than 5-10 sessions at intervals of 1-2 months.
recommendedFor: Individuals with Ota nevus (bluish-gray pigment around the eyes)
Individuals concerned about the aesthetic appearance of café-au-lait spots
Individuals seeking stepwise treatment for congenital pigment lesions
Individuals who can follow a long-term treatment plan
Individuals wanting treatment after an accurate diagnosis

faq.a: Yes, the Q-Switched laser can gradually break down the melanocytes in the dermis.

faq.q: Can it be done from a young age?
faq.a: Infants and children can undergo the procedure, but the timing is determined after consultation with medical staff.
Depending on the size and depth of the lesions, it is conducted more than 5-15 times at intervals of 1-2 months.
It will significantly lighten, but complete removal may be difficult. Setting realistic goals is important.

redness.name: Redness · Telangiectasia
redness.tagline: PDL vascular-specific laser precisely targets only hemoglobin
redness.intro: Facial redness and telangiectasia (red spider veins) on the nose and cheeks occur when blood vessels are abnormally dilated. The 595nm PDL laser selectively absorbs hemoglobin, protecting normal tissue while soothing abnormal vessels.
redness.approach: 1) Selective targeting of hemoglobin with VBeam's 595nm PDL, 2) Epidermal protection with DCD cooling, 3) Pulse width adjustment according to the thickness and depth of the capillaries, 4) 3-5 sessions at intervals of 4-6 weeks to expect cumulative effects.
recommendedFor: Those concerned about chronic redness on the nose, cheeks, and chin
Those with visible telangiectasia (red spider veins)
Those whose faces often turn red due to stress or temperature changes
Those seeking a safe treatment for sensitive skin
Those who can receive regular maintenance care

faq.a: You will feel a soothing effect immediately after the treatment, and permanent changes will appear cumulatively over sessions.
It feels cool and slightly prickly due to DCD cooling. Anesthesia cream is not mandatory.
The blood vessels themselves are removed, but new capillaries may form, so maintenance treatments every 1-2 years are recommended.

faq.q: What care is needed after treatment?
faq.a: Avoid saunas, intense exercise, and UV exposure for one week, and ensure thorough moisturizing and sun protection.

acne-active.name: Teenage and Adult Acne
acne-active.tagline: Light and heat treatment that cares for both sebaceous glands and acne bacteria
acne-active.intro: Teenage acne is primarily caused by hormones and excess sebum, while adult acne is influenced by a combination of stress, lifestyle habits, and hormonal imbalances. Both medication and antibiotics, as well as light and heat treatment combined with pore cleansing, can reduce recurrence.
acne-active.approach: 1) Cleansing sebum and dead skin cells in the pores with CUREJET, 2) Calming P. acnes bacteria and sebaceous glands simultaneously with Gold PTT, 3) Concurrent medication prescription, 4) Cumulative effect with 3-5 treatments at 6-week intervals + lifestyle management.
recommendedFor: Those struggling with chronic and recurrent acne
Those who feel burdened relying solely on medication
Those with excessive sebum and clogged pores
Those who prefer treatments with no downtime
Those who want to prevent recurrence with regular care

faq.q: Should I combine it with medication?
faq.a: When the activity is severe, combining medication (topical agents or oral medication) can lead to faster results.

faq.q: How long does the treatment take?
faq.a: CUREJET takes about 30-40 minutes + Gold PTT takes about 50 minutes. Both treatments can be performed on the same day.
Both treatments have minimal pain and almost no downtime.
Regular maintenance treatments + lifestyle habits (sleep, diet, stress management) are key.

acne-pigment.name: Acne Pigmentation
acne-pigment.tagline: Step-by-step care for PIE (red spots) and PIH (brown spots) left after acne
acne-pigment.intro: There are two types of pigmentation that remain after acne subsides. PIE (red spots, post-inflammatory erythema) is vascular, while PIH (brown pigmentation, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation) is melanogenic. Each requires separate care with different lasers for effective treatment.
acne-pigment.approach: 1) PIE (red spots) is treated with VBeam 595nm PDL for vascular calming, 2) PIH (brown spots) is treated with Clarity II or Fotona StarWalker toning for pigment breakdown, 3) Step-by-step improvement with 3-5 sessions at intervals of 4-6 weeks.
recommendedFor: Those whose acne has subsided but have lingering red marks
Those concerned about brown pigmentation after acne
Those who have visible marks but not scars
Those with marks that show even with makeup
Those who can receive step-by-step improvement

faq.q: How can I distinguish between PIE and PIH?
faq.a: Medical professionals accurately diagnose using glass plate pressure tests and Wood's lamp examinations. PIE fades when pressed, while PIH remains unchanged.

faq.q: Should I receive both treatments together?
faq.a: If both are present, the two treatments will be distributed across sessions.
Both treatments have almost no downtime.
If new acne forms, pigmentation may return, so managing active acne is a priority.

acne-scar.name: Acne Scars
acne-scar.tagline: Stepwise reconstruction of depressed scars — combination of fractional and microneedling
acne-scar.intro: Acne scars require different treatments depending on their type (ice pick, boxcar, rolling). Deep scars need stepwise reconstruction with fractional CO2 laser, while moderate scars require insulated microneedling RF, among other combinations.
acne-scar.approach: 1) Diagnosis of scar type and establishment of treatment plan, 2) Reconstruction of depressed scars with Capri (CO2) fractional, 3) Dermal regeneration assistance with Secret RF microneedling, 4) Stepwise progress with 3-5 sessions at intervals of 1-2 months.
recommendedFor: Individuals with acne scars (ice pick, boxcar, rolling)
Those who can undergo multiple treatments stepwise
Those who can tolerate a recovery period of 5-10 days
Individuals who want to improve skin texture as a long-term plan
Those whose active acne has settled

faq.a: Capri CO2 takes about 5-10 days, while Secret RF has redness and scabbing for about 2-3 days.
With stepwise treatments, improvement of about 70-80% can be expected, but complete removal is often difficult.
Numbing cream is essential. There will be a prickly and warm sensation during the procedure.

faq.q: Can I receive treatment if I have active acne?
faq.a: It is safer to receive treatment after the active acne has settled. We first calm it down with medication and light therapy.

pores.name: Pores
pores.tagline: Shrink and rebuild enlarged pores + Cleansing inside the pores
pores.intro: There are various reasons for enlarged pores. Excess sebum, decreased collagen, aging, and repeated irritation work together. By cleansing inside the pores and regenerating the dermis, you can achieve a smooth texture.
pores.approach: 1) Cleansing sebum and dead skin cells inside the pores with CUREJET, 2) Shrinking pore walls and regenerating the dermis with Carpri (CO2) or Secret RF, 3) Cumulative effects with regular care every 3-5 sessions at 1-month intervals.
recommendedFor: Those with enlarged pores on the nose and cheeks
Those prone to clogged pores due to excess sebum
Those whose makeup settles into the pores
Those with enlarged pores due to decreased collagen
Those who need regular texture management

faq.a: The pores themselves will not disappear, but we can improve their appearance by tightening enlarged pores.

faq.q: Is there any effect from just receiving CUREJET?
faq.a: There is immediate texture improvement, but fundamental improvement of enlarged pores requires dermal regeneration treatments.
CUREJET 0 days, Secret RF 2-3 days, Carpri CO2 5-10 days.

faq.q: What is the regular care cycle?
faq.a: CUREJET once or twice a month, dermal regeneration treatments every 1-2 months followed by maintenance treatments.

athletes-foot.name: Athlete's foot
athletes-foot.tagline: Accurate diagnosis and treatment of fungal infections without recurrence
athletes-foot.intro: Athlete's foot (tinea pedis) is a skin fungal infection that can lead to recurrence and chronicity if self-treatment is repeated without an accurate diagnosis. Treatment with antifungal medication begins after confirming the fungus through tests such as KOH examination.
athletes-foot.approach: 1) Diagnosis by confirming the fungus with KOH examination, 2) Prescription of antifungal topical agents and oral medications tailored to the area and symptoms, 3) Guidance on lifestyle habits to prevent recurrence (ventilation, foot hygiene, management of socks and shoes).
recommendedFor: Those with itching, cracking, or scaling between the toes
Those who do not improve with over-the-counter medications
Those with frequent recurrences
Those who want an accurate diagnosis
Those who want to prevent transmission to family or cohabitants

faq.q: What is the difference from over-the-counter medications?
faq.a: Using medications without an accurate diagnosis can lead to using the wrong medication or causing irritation. The prescribed antifungal medication is safer and more effective.
Depending on the area and severity, it can take 2 weeks to several months. Even after improvement, continuing the medication for a certain period is necessary to reduce recurrence.
It can be transmitted through sharing towels or shoes. Hygiene management within the family is important.
Make sure to dry your feet well, manage socks and shoes to ensure good ventilation, and cleanse after using public baths or swimming pools.

psoriasis.name: Psoriasis · Tinea
psoriasis.tagline: Long-term management plan for chronic inflammatory diseases
psoriasis.intro: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory disease caused by immune system abnormalities, while tinea is a fungal infection. The two conditions may appear similar, making accurate diagnosis important, and each requires different treatment approaches.
psoriasis.approach: 1) Accurate diagnosis (KOH test, biopsy, etc.), 2) Psoriasis is treated with topical agents, phototherapy, and systemic medications in a stepwise manner, 3) Tinea is treated with antifungal therapy, 4) As a chronic condition, it requires a long-term management plan to prevent recurrence.
recommendedFor: Individuals with recurring scaly rashes on the scalp, elbows, knees, etc.
Individuals whose condition worsens due to stress or seasonal changes
Individuals needing accurate diagnosis and long-term management
Individuals who have not improved with existing topical agents
Individuals with accompanying systemic symptoms

faq.a: Psoriasis is difficult to cure and is a chronic condition that requires long-term management. Symptoms can be managed to a level where they are almost absent.
If there is a family history, the likelihood of occurrence is higher, but environmental and stress factors also play a significant role.
Stress, infections, medications, trauma, alcohol and smoking, and dry climates are exacerbating factors.
Psoriasis is not contagious. Tinea, being a fungal infection, can be contagious.

atopy.name: Atopy
atopy.tagline: Step-by-step treatment and lifestyle management focused on skin barrier recovery
atopy.intro: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that occurs due to a weakened skin barrier. It is characterized by recurring itching, rashes, and dryness, and both medication and skin barrier recovery along with environmental and lifestyle management are important.
atopy.approach: 1) Daily care focused on moisturizing and skin barrier recovery, 2) Prescription of topical steroids and immunosuppressants tailored to the stage of inflammation, 3) Antihistamines for itch control, 4) Guidance on environmental, dietary, and stress management.
recommendedFor: Those who have experienced recurring itching and rashes since childhood
Individuals with chronically dry and rough skin
Those who experience cycles of improvement and worsening with existing topical steroids
Individuals who need comprehensive management rather than simple prescriptions
Those with a family history of allergic diseases

faq.q: Does it not go away even when you become an adult?
faq.a: Atopy that started in childhood can continue into adulthood, but with step-by-step management, symptoms can be maintained at a nearly absent level.
When used under medical supervision for a short period and at appropriate strength, they are safe. Self-judgment to discontinue or overuse should be avoided.
At least 1-2 times a day, immediately after bathing is most effective.
Generally, excessive restriction is not needed except for allergy foods confirmed by testing.

burns.name: Burns
burns.tagline: Post-burn care aimed at minimizing scars
burns.intro: Burns are treated differently depending on their depth (1st, 2nd, 3rd degree). Even after first aid, scars and pigmentation may remain, making care and treatments at each recovery stage important. Early intervention before the scar hardens greatly influences the outcome.
burns.approach: 1) For urgent burns, go to the emergency room, then proceed with scar and pigmentation care after recovery, 2) For pigmentation, use toning, 3) For depressed scars, use fractional CO2, 4) For raised hypertrophic scars, use steroid injections, etc., in a stepwise approach.
recommendedFor: Those with scars or pigmentation remaining after burns
Those who have recovered but are concerned about appearance
Those struggling with hypertrophic or keloid scars
Those who want to reduce scars with early intervention
Those who can receive stepwise care

faq.q: What to do for urgent burns?
faq.a: Run cool water for more than 15 minutes, then go to the emergency room or dermatology. Self-treatment (such as with soybean paste or toothpaste) is strictly prohibited.
It varies depending on the depth, area, and recovery process. Early intervention can minimize scars.
After the wound has completely healed. Usually, scar care starts 6 weeks to 3 months later.
They are treated stepwise with steroid injections, silicone sheets, and compression therapy.

hair-loss.name: Hair Loss
hair-loss.tagline: Diagnosis by Cause and Scalp & Hair Strengthening Treatment
hair-loss.intro: Hair loss is caused by a combination of various factors such as genetics, hormones, stress, and nutrition. A comprehensive approach involving accurate diagnosis of the cause, medication, injections, scalp care, and lifestyle adjustments is necessary for effectiveness.
hair-loss.approach: 1) Hair examination and scalp condition analysis, 2) For androgenetic alopecia, medications (finasteride, minoxidil), 3) Follicle stimulation with mesotherapy, PRP, and exosome injections, 4) Concurrent scalp care and nutritional management.
recommendedFor: Individuals whose hairline and crown appear to be thinning
Those with a family history of androgenetic alopecia
Individuals experiencing temporary hair loss after childbirth, dieting, or stress
Those who want to actively manage in the early stages
Individuals who can undergo medication and procedures together

faq.q: When will I see the effects of the medication?
faq.a: Changes are usually seen after 3 to 6 months, and consistent use for over a year is required.

faq.q: Are there side effects of the medication?
faq.a: Medications related to male hormones should be used under medical supervision. Decisions are made after consulting about potential side effects.
Mesotherapy, PRP, and exosomes can help stimulate hair follicles, and synergy is expected when combined with medication.

faq.q: Can female hair loss be treated?
faq.a: A separate diagnosis is needed as the causes differ. Hormone tests and iron tests are conducted to identify the causes.
